mainTopic: Explaining the משנה of two sisters who fall to two brothers for יבום: רבי יוחנן's difficulty, the order of falling, the מחלוקת about brothers who married first, and why the משנה repeats earlier rules
overview: The גמרא continues discussing a משנה about two brothers married to two sisters who die, so that the sisters fall for יבום to the surviving brothers. רבי יוחנן had said, 'Sisters, I do not know who taught it,' because he could not explain why both sisters must do חליצה and not יבום. The גמרא offers him five possible explanations: two kinds of rabbinic decree, the view of רבי אלעזר, the view of רבי יוסי הגלילי, and a case of doubt about which sister fell first. Each is turned down, either from the wording of the משנה, from רבי יוחנן's own position, or from how the משנה is written. Next, רב פפא explains the order of falling in the case where one sister is an ערוה to one brother. The גמרא then brings a ברייתא with three reports about brothers who married before asking בית דין, and explains that רבי שמעון holds בית שמאי and בית הלל did not argue at all. Finally, the גמרא asks why the משנה repeats rules already taught elsewhere and answers with a צריכא. It then begins the same question about איסור מצוה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה teaches what is done from the start
steps.stepSummary: The word 'חולצות' describes the required first step, not a last resort after something went wrong.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches what is done from the outset.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes answering a question that began just before this section. It says the משנה's word 'חולצות' tells us what must be done right from the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone suggested the משנה might allow a different arrangement. The answer is that the משנה is describing the plan from the beginning: חליצה is the path, not a backup option.

keyTerms.meaning: From the outset; the proper way to act from the start
They perform חליצה (the release ceremony instead of יבום)

phrases.english: It teaches the case of what is done from the outset.
phrases.notes: This answers the question asked just before. The word being explained is 'חולצות' in the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an answer to a question raised before this section
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the wording of the משנה precisely
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה requires חליצה as the first and proper course of action

steps.title: Maybe the ban on levirate marriage is only a rabbinic decree
steps.stepSummary: The challenger suggests that רבי יוחנן could have said יבום is banned only because of a rabbinic decree, out of fear that he would do חליצה with the first sister first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him say to him: it is a decree, in case he goes ahead and does חליצה with the first sister first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן did not offer a simpler reason for the ruling: a rabbinic decree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he did חליצה with the first sister, marrying the second would be forbidden, since she is the sister of a woman he did חליצה with. So maybe the רבנן banned יבום across the board to prevent that mistake. That would mean יבום is not forbidden here by the basic law.

keyTerms.meaning: And let him say to him; why not answer this way?
A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard
He went ahead and did חליצה first

phrases.english: And let him say to him: it is a decree,
lest he go ahead and perform חליצה
with the first sister first!
phrases.notes: After that, marrying the second sister would be forbidden, because she is the sister of a woman he did חליצה with.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֵימָא לֵיהּ: גְּזֵירָה דִּלְמָא קְדֵים וַחֲלֵיץ לְרִאשׁוֹנָה בְּרֵישָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new possible reason for the משנה's ruling
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's statement that he does not know who taught the case of sisters
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rabbinic decree could explain the ruling, so רבי יוחנן need not have found the משנה puzzling

steps.title: 'They may not do levirate marriage' means none at all
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says 'ולא מתייבמות', which shows that the law of יבום does not apply here at all. A mere decree would not explain that wording.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches 'and they do not do יבום', which means there is no law of יבום here at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the decree idea by pointing to the exact words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A decree would only stop יבום as a safeguard. The משנה's flat statement 'ולא מתייבמות' shows that יבום simply does not exist in this case. So the problem is basic, not just a protective fence.

keyTerms.meaning: And they do not do יבום

phrases.english: It teaches 'and they do not do levirate marriage,'
meaning there is no law of levirate marriage here at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the decree suggestion of step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the משנה's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ban might be only a rabbinic safeguard
steps.terutzMaskana: The wording shows יבום does not apply here at all

steps.title: Maybe the decree is out of fear a brother might die
steps.stepSummary: The challenger suggests another decree: maybe יבום was banned in case a brother dies, which would cause the מצוה of יבום to be lost.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him say to him: it is a decree in case he dies, and it is forbidden to cancel the מצוה of יבום.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second possible reason for the ruling: a safeguard against a brother dying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that if a brother died, things could end with the מצוה of יבום being cancelled. To avoid that, the רבנן might have banned יבום from the start. That would explain the משנה, so רבי יוחנן would have no reason to call it puzzling.

phrases.english: And let him say to him: it is a decree lest he die,
and it is forbidden to cancel the מצוה of levirate marriage!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another alternative reason, after the first was rejected
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's statement that he does not know who taught the case of sisters
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A decree about possible death could explain the ruling instead

steps.title: רבי יוחנן is not concerned about death
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן does not make rulings based on the chance that someone might die, so he could not use this reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן is not concerned about death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the second suggestion by pointing to a known position of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A decree based on 'maybe he will die' only works for someone who worries about that possibility. רבי יוחנן does not, so this reason does not fit his view.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan is not concerned about death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing to the speaker's known general position
steps.terutzMaskana: This decree does not fit רבי יוחנן's view

steps.title: Maybe the משנה follows רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The challenger suggests the משנה follows רבי אלעזר: once a woman was forbidden to him even for one moment, she stays forbidden forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him say to him: it is רבי אלעזר, who said that once she stood before him forbidden for one moment, she is forbidden to him forever.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a third way to explain the משנה: it might follow the view of רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר holds that a single moment of being forbidden makes a יבמה forbidden forever. At some moment in this case, the sister was forbidden, so by his view the ban would be permanent. That would explain the ruling, so רבי יוחנן would have no reason to call the משנה puzzling.

phrases.english: And let him say to him: it follows Rabbi Elazar,
who said: once she stood before him
for one moment as forbidden,
she is forbidden to him forever.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third alternative explanation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Placing the משנה under רבי אלעזר would explain the ruling another way

steps.title: The later clause names רבי אלעזר, so the first clause is not his
steps.stepSummary: Since the later part of the משנה names רבי אלעזר outright, the earlier part, which has no name, must not be his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the later part is רבי אלעזר, the first part is not רבי אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the third suggestion based on how the משנה is built.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the משנה names רבי אלעזר in its later clause, that shows his view is a separate opinion. So the unnamed first clause, where our ruling appears, cannot belong to him.

keyTerms.meaning: The later clause of a משנה
The first clause of a משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as rejecting רבי אלעזר's view. The גמרא only says our part of the משנה is not his, because he is named separately later on.

phrases.english: Since the latter clause is Rabbi Elazar,
the first clause is not Rabbi Elazar.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּסֵיפָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר רֵישָׁא לָאו רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Inference from the structure of the משנה
steps.terutzMaskana: The first clause cannot be attributed to רבי אלעזר

steps.title: Maybe both sisters fell at the exact same moment
steps.stepSummary: The challenger suggests the case is one where both sisters fell for יבום at exactly the same moment, following רבי יוסי הגלילי, who holds that such precise timing is possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him say to them: they fell at the same moment, and it follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, who said it is possible to be exact.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a fourth way to explain the משנה: the case involves both sisters falling for יבום at the very same instant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both brothers died at the exact same moment, each sister was forbidden right when she fell, so יבום never applied to either one. That only works if we accept רבי יוסי הגלילי's view that two events can happen at precisely the same moment.

keyTerms.meaning: It is possible to be exact (that two events happen at precisely the same instant)
Fell (came before the brother for יבום)

phrases.english: And let him say to them: where they fell at the same moment,
and it follows Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
who said: it is possible to be exact!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A fourth alternative explanation
steps.kashyaTarget: How the case in the משנה is defined
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Limiting the case to falling at the same moment would explain the ruling and remove רבי יוחנן's difficulty

steps.title: An unnamed משנה does not follow רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: The תנא never wrote an unnamed משנה following רבי יוסי הגלילי, so our unnamed משנה cannot be his view.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא did not teach us an unnamed משנה following רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects this suggestion with a general rule about how the משנה was written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An unnamed משנה is meant to state the accepted law. רבי יוסי הגלילי's view is never stated that way; it always appears with his name attached. Since our משנה has no name, it cannot follow him.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught without a name (an unnamed משנה)
The author or teacher of the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: Four suggested explanations have now been turned down. The decree ideas fail because of the משנה's wording and because רבי יוחנן does not worry about death. The other two fail because of how the משנה is written. One more suggestion follows in step 10, and step 12 draws the conclusion.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common tool of the גמרא: an unnamed משנה is not placed under a minority opinion that is normally stated with a name.

phrases.english: The תנא did not teach us an unnamed teaching
in accordance with Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סְתַם לַן תַּנָּא כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: A general rule about unnamed משניות
steps.terutzMaskana: The unnamed משנה cannot follow רבי יוסי הגלילי

steps.title: Maybe we just don't know which sister fell first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests another way to explain the משנה: the brothers died one after the other, but nobody knows which sister fell for יבום first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let רבי יוחנן answer that we do not know which sister fell first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a new way to explain why the משנה forbids both sisters. Maybe it is a case of doubt about which one fell first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answers were rejected because they depended on someone dying, on רבי אלעזר, or on רבי יוסי הגלילי. This suggestion avoids all of those. If one sister really fell first she would be permitted, but since we don't know which one it was, both are forbidden out of doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: And let him say to him (a suggested answer)

phrases.english: And let him say to him:
phrases.notes: He means: let רבי יוחנן give this answer to רבי יוסי בר חנינא.

phrases.english: that we do not know which one fell first.
phrases.notes: 'Fell' means the sister became bound to the brother for יבום when her husband died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the רבי יוסי הגלילי approach is rejected, a new explanation of the משנה's case is offered.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that he cannot explain the משנה's ruling about sisters
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A simple case of doubt about which sister fell first would explain why both are forbidden, so there should be no difficulty.

steps.title: The rule 'they must divorce' does not fit a case of doubt
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that brothers who married before asking must divorce. In a case of doubt, the brother who married second could argue that his marriage may be permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, how can the משנה say that if they married first they must divorce? The brother who married first is told: 'Who allowed you?' But the one who married second can say: 'My brother took one sister, so I am taking the other, who may be the permitted one.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the doubt explanation by pointing to the משנה's ruling that both brothers must divorce. In a case of doubt, that ruling does not work for the second brother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first brother to marry acted on a doubt, so he clearly did wrong. The second brother has an argument: once one sister was taken, the sister he took might be the one who was really permitted. The משנה sounds like there is no such argument, so the case cannot be one of doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: They went ahead and married (before asking בית דין)

phrases.english: If so,
does that fit what it teaches: if they went ahead and married, they must divorce?
Granted, the first,
we say to him: who permitted her to you?
But the second, he can say:
My fellow did יבום with the second,
I am doing יבום with the first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the doubt explanation from step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Contradiction with another clause of the same משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A case of doubt about which sister fell first would explain the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A case of doubt does not fit the ruling that both brothers must divorce, so this explanation fails.

steps.title: This is why רבי יוחנן said he doesn't know who taught 'sisters'
steps.stepSummary: Since every possible explanation has failed, the גמרא concludes that this is what רבי יוחנן meant when he said he does not know who taught the case of sisters.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is what he meant when he said: 'Sisters, I do not know who taught it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wraps up the whole discussion. רבי יוחנן's puzzling statement is now explained.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each attempt failed: the chance that someone dies, רבי אלעזר, רבי יוסי הגלילי, and a case of doubt. No good explanation is left for the משנה's ruling. So רבי יוחנן honestly said he could not identify who taught it.

keyTerms.meaning: That is what he meant when he said

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's ruling that both sisters are forbidden cannot easily be explained by any timing scenario. That is why רבי יוחנן said, 'Sisters, I do not know who taught it.'

phrases.english: That is what he said to him:
phrases.notes: He is רבי יוחנן, speaking to רבי יוסי בר חנינא.

phrases.english: Sisters, I do not know who taught them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the failure of all the attempts, ending with step 11.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: No explanation fits the משנה's ruling about sisters, which is why רבי יוחנן did not know who taught it.

steps.title: Testing the משנה's case of a sister who is an ערוה to one brother
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה: if one sister is an ערוה to one brother, he may marry her sister, and the other brother is forbidden to both. It begins to analyze this by imagining that his mother-in-law fell first.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: If one of them was forbidden to one brother as an ערוה, he is forbidden to her and permitted to her sister, and the second brother is forbidden to both. You might think this means his mother-in-law fell first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the משנה and starts to figure out its case. This step sets up the next question by suggesting that the forbidden woman, his mother-in-law, fell for יבום first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ערוה sister is completely forbidden to her relative, so she creates no יבום bond with him, and he may marry her sister. The other brother is related to neither sister, yet he is forbidden to both. The גמרא now tests what order of falling would explain this, starting with the idea that the mother-in-law fell first.

keyTerms.meaning: It would enter your mind (a first assumption)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Sister' here means one of the two widows, and the brothers are the יבמין. The ערוה problem is only for one brother, who is related to that widow, for example because she is his wife's mother.

phrases.english: We learned:
If one of them was
forbidden to one of the brothers with an ערוה prohibition,
he is forbidden to her and permitted to her sister,
and the second brother is forbidden to both of them.
It would enter your mind
that his mother-in-law fell first.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָיְתָה אַחַת מֵהֶן אֲסוּרָה עַל הָאֶחָד אִיסּוּר עֶרְוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the finished discussion about sisters to the next clause of the same משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's clause about a sister who is an ערוה to one brother
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The גמרא sets up a first assumption about the order of falling, to test whether it fits the משנה's ruling.

steps.title: Why can't the mother-in-law become permitted again?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the other brother is forbidden to both sisters. The son-in-law could do יבום with the sister who is not his mother-in-law first. Then the mother-in-law would be free again for the other brother, like an ordinary יבמה who was permitted, then forbidden, then permitted again.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why? Let the son-in-law go first and do יבום with the sister who is not his mother-in-law. Then, for the other brother, the mother-in-law is like a יבמה who was permitted, then forbidden, then permitted again. She should go back to being permitted, as she was at first!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's rule that the second brother is forbidden to both sisters. It suggests a simple way for the mother-in-law to become permitted to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 began by picturing a case where the mother-in-law fell first. In that case she was permitted to the other brother at first. When her sister fell too, the זיקה to her sister made her forbidden to him. Once the son-in-law does יבום with her sister, that זיקה is gone, so she should go back to being permitted. The משנה says he is forbidden to both, so something must be wrong with this picture.

keyTerms.meaning: son-in-law (here, the brother whose mother-in-law is one of the sisters)
his mother-in-law, who is an ערוה to him
who was permitted, then forbidden, then permitted again

steps.confusionAlert: The woman is called 'his mother-in-law' only because of the first brother, the son-in-law. To the other brother she is not related at all. She is simply a יבמה whose sister also fell to him.

phrases.english: And why?
phrases.notes: He means: why should the other brother be forbidden to both sisters, as the משנה says?

phrases.english: Let the son-in-law stand up and do יבום
with the one who is not his mother-in-law, first,
and then his mother-in-law, as far as the other brother is concerned, would be
phrases.notes: She is the first brother's mother-in-law. To the other brother she is just a regular יבמה.

phrases.english: like a יבמה who was permitted and then forbidden
and then became permitted again,
so she should go back to her first permitted status!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the analysis begun in step 13, which pictured the mother-in-law falling first.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that the second brother is forbidden to both sisters
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the mother-in-law fell first, she was permitted to the other brother at first. After the son-in-law does יבום with her sister, she should return to that original permission.

steps.title: רב פפא: The other sister fell first
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the משנה is talking about a case where the sister who is not the mother-in-law fell for יבום first. So the mother-in-law was forbidden to the other brother from the very start and never had any permission to return to.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The case is where the one who is not his mother-in-law fell for יבום first.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question by changing the order of events in the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the non-mother-in-law fell first, the other brother already had a זיקה to her. When the mother-in-law fell afterward, she was forbidden to him from the moment she fell, as the sister of his זקוקה. Since she was never permitted to him, the rule of 'returning to her first permission' does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: who fell, meaning she became bound for יבום

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the order in which the women fell for יבום decides whether a woman can ever become permitted again.

phrases.english: רב פפא said:
The case is where she fell for יבום
the one who is not his mother-in-law, first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The mother-in-law fell first, so she was once permitted to the other brother and should become permitted again.
steps.terutzMaskana: The other sister fell first, so the mother-in-law was forbidden to the other brother from the start and can never become permitted.

steps.title: Three opinions on brothers who married before asking
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אליעזר's words in the משנה and brings a ברייתא with three views. רבי אליעזר says בית שמאי let them stay married and בית הלל say divorce. רבי שמעון says they may stay married. אבא שאול says it is the other way around: בית הלל were the lenient ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: רבי אליעזר says, בית שמאי say, and so on. It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר says that בית שמאי say they may stay married and בית הלל say they must divorce. רבי שמעון says they may stay married. אבא שאול says: בית הלל were the lenient ones in this matter, for בית שמאי say they must divorce and בית הלל say they may stay married.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה about brothers who married the sisters without asking בית דין. It brings a ברייתא that lays out the different opinions in full, to set up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה had said that such brothers must divorce. רבי אליעזר disagrees and says this is really a מחלוקת between בית שמאי and בית הלל. The ברייתא shows that אבא שאול remembers the מחלוקת in the opposite way, and that רבי שמעון gives a ruling without naming either side.

keyTerms.meaning: they may keep them, meaning they may stay married
they must send them out, meaning they must divorce

phrases.english: רבי אליעזר says:
בית שמאי say, and so on.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from our משנה, about brothers who married the sisters before asking בית דין.

phrases.english: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר says,
בית שמאי say: They may stay married,
and בית הלל say: They must divorce.
רבי שמעון says: They may stay married.
אבא שאול says:

phrases.aramaic: קַל הָיָה לָהֶם לְבֵית הִלֵּל בְּדָבָר זֶה,
phrases.english: בית הלל were the lenient ones in this matter,
for בית שמאי say: They must divorce,
and בית הלל say: They may stay married.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים וְכוּ׳. תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are three reports: רבי אליעזר says בית שמאי are lenient, אבא שאול says בית הלל are lenient, and רבי שמעון simply rules they may stay married.

steps.title: Whose side is רבי שמעון on?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי שמעון adds. If he follows בית שמאי, he is saying the same thing as רבי אליעזר. If he follows בית הלל, he is saying the same thing as אבא שאול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון is like whom? If he follows בית שמאי, that is just רבי אליעזר's view. If he follows בית הלל, that is just אבא שאול's view!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי שמעון's opinion in the ברייתא. It looks like he adds nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both רבי אליעזר and אבא שאול already have one side saying 'they may stay married'. So רבי שמעון's 'they may stay married' seems to match one of them. Then why is he listed as a separate opinion?

keyTerms.meaning: like whom, meaning whose view he follows

phrases.english: רבי שמעון holds like whom?
If like בית שמאי,
that is the same as רבי אליעזר.
If like בית הלל,
that is the same as אבא שאול!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions one of the opinions in the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's opinion in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Either way, his view matches one of the other two תנאים, so it seems he adds nothing.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: There was no dispute at all
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי שמעון holds a third view. בית שמאי and בית הלל never argued about this, and both agree the brothers may stay married.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: בית שמאי and בית הלל did not argue about this matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון is not siding with either report. He says there was no מחלוקת at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר and אבא שאול each say one house was lenient and the other strict. רבי שמעון says both houses agreed to the lenient ruling. That is why he gives his ruling without naming either house.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three views about brothers who married before asking. רבי אליעזר says בית שמאי let them stay married. אבא שאול says בית הלל let them stay married. רבי שמעון says both houses agreed they may stay married.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
phrases.english: בית שמאי and בית הלל did not argue
about this matter.
phrases.notes: He means both houses agreed: they may stay married.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וּבֵית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the opinion as a separate third view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון follows one side of the מחלוקת, so he repeats רבי אליעזר or אבא שאול.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון holds there was no מחלוקת. Both houses agreed the brothers may stay married.

steps.title: Didn't we already learn this rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case where one sister is an ערוה to one brother. It asks why this is needed, since an earlier משנה already taught that when a woman's sister is an ערוה to the יבם, she may do חליצה or יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'If one of them was forbidden as an ערוה...' But we already learned this once before: when her sister is also her fellow יבמה, she either does חליצה or does יבום!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה for repeating itself. The same rule seems to have been taught already in an earlier משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says the brother is forbidden to the sister who is his ערוה, but he may marry her sister. An earlier משנה already said that when two sisters fall to one יבם and one is his ערוה, the other one may do חליצה or יבום. So why does the משנה need to say it again?

keyTerms.meaning: Her fellow יבמה, a woman who fell to the same יבם

phrases.english: If one of them was, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes our משנה: one sister is an ערוה to one brother, so he can't marry her but may marry her sister.

phrases.english: But we already learned this one time:
Her sister, when she is her fellow יבמה,
phrases.notes: This is an earlier משנה (יבמות כ). The sister who is an ערוה to the יבם is also waiting for him.

phrases.english: she either does חליצה or does יבום!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the מחלוקת about רבי אליעזר and רבי שמעון to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's clause that a brother is forbidden to his ערוה but permitted to her sister.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same rule was already taught in an earlier משנה, so repeating it seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Both places are needed because of the second brother
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that both משניות are needed. From the earlier משנה alone, we might forbid יבום here, because a second brother might also marry. From our משנה alone, we might permit it only because the second brother's behavior shows it is forbidden for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is necessary. If it had taught us only there, I would say it is allowed there because there is no second brother to worry about. But here, where there is a second brother to worry about, I would say no. And if it had taught us only here, I would say it is allowed because the second brother shows by staying away that this is forbidden. But there, where there is no second brother, I would say no. So both are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a צריכא: each משנה teaches something we could not learn from the other one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier case there is only one יבם, so there is no worry about anyone else. Here there are two brothers, so we might have forbidden even the first brother, in case the second brother also marries. But in our case the second brother stays away, and that shows people the sister is forbidden to him. Without that sign, as in the earlier case, we might have forbidden it. So each case has its own reason for doubt, and both must be taught.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary: both teachings are needed
To make a rabbinic decree (a גזירה)
Shows, makes it clear to people

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two worries. The first is that the second brother might also marry. The second is the opposite: the second brother staying away helps, because it shows people the sister is forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: A צריכא answer shows that each repeated teaching covers a case the other could not: one case has a second brother and one does not, and each has a different reason we might have been strict.

phrases.english: It is necessary,
for if it had taught us only there,
I would say it is allowed because there is no reason to make a decree because of a second brother,
but here,
where there is reason to make a decree because of the second brother,
I would say no.
And if it had taught us only here,
I would say it is allowed because there is a second brother who shows,
but there, where there is no second brother,
I would say no.
So it is necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of why the משנה repeats itself.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכא: each source teaches a case the other could not.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the earlier משנה alone, we would forbid יבום when there are two brothers. From our משנה alone, we would forbid it when there is only one brother.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both משניות are needed. יבום with the sister who is not an ערוה is allowed whether there is a second brother or not.

steps.title: Isn't the case of איסור מצוה also already taught?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next clause of the משנה about איסור מצוה and starts asking the same question: we already learned this too. The source it has in mind is quoted on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'If she was forbidden by an איסור מצוה...' But we already learned this as well:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next question. It quotes the משנה's case of איסור מצוה and begins to say this was already taught, and the earlier source comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה, when one sister is forbidden to a brother by an איסור מצוה or an איסור קדושה, her sister must do חליצה and not יבום. The גמרא now asks the same kind of question as before: this rule also seems to have been taught already.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition from a מצוה, a lighter level than an ערוה
Etc.: the quote of the משנה continues

phrases.english: A prohibition from a מצוה, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the next part of our משנה: if one sister has this kind of prohibition, her sister does חליצה, not יבום.

phrases.english: We already learned this as well:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same kind of question as step 19, now on the next clause of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's clause about איסור מצוה and איסור קדושה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This rule also seems to have been taught already in an earlier משנה, so repeating it seems unnecessary. The earlier source is quoted on the next amud.
